evals.prompt: I already scaffolded a Scaffold HBAR app (packages/nextjs present, yarn workspaces). Help me create an ASSERT-only hedera-harness recipe under .harness/ for an HCS proof-wall feature called proof-wall: users browse a public message wall without a wallet, and posting requires connecting a wallet. No Solidity.
evals.expected_output: A grilling session that asks one question at a time with a recommended answer, looks up project facts instead of asking, waits for shared understanding before writing files, then emits a minimal schemaVersion 3 recipe at .harness/spec.yaml with a baseline install command, plus .harness/prd.md and validators, leaving v3 defaults commented out and omitting skills:.
assertions: The output satisfies: Follows grilling protocol: one question at a time / recommended answer
The output satisfies: Does not write files until shared understanding is confirmed
The output includes schemaVersion: 3: Recipe declares schemaVersion 3
The output includes .harness/spec.yaml: Writes the recipe to the project-centric .harness/ path
The output satisfies: Baseline includes a command literally named install
The output satisfies: Leaves v3-defaulted plumbing out of the recipe rather than restating it
The output satisfies: Does not emit keys removed in schema v3 (seed, generator, logging, extend, contract, skills)
The output satisfies: Names HCS / product skill discovery without listing skills: in the recipe
The output satisfies: Keeps the run blind / separates PRD from evaluate checklist
The output satisfies: Names doctor and/or check-spec.sh as the completion criterion

evals.prompt: Deepen my existing proof-wall harness recipe to EVALUATE. Derive evaluate-checklist assertions from the PRD journeys (browse without wallet; wallet-gated post).
evals.expected_output: An evaluate checklist at .harness/eval.json with numbered E-prefixed assertions carrying statement and howToVerify, a fail-closed evaluationRules posture, both eval and validator.enabled set in the recipe, and a reminder that the PRD must stay blind.
assertions: The output satisfies: Uses stable numbered assertion ids (E1, E2, ...)
The output includes howToVerify: Assertions carry concrete browser verification steps
The output satisfies: Enables both eval and validator.enabled — either alone is misconfigured
The output uses the v3 default evaluate checklist path
The output satisfies: Evaluate checklist keeps a fail-closed posture
The output satisfies: Reminds the user not to leak checklist detail into the PRD
The output satisfies: Does not hand-write validator CLI flags or model names; the agent preset owns those

evals.prompt: When should I enable chainValidation for my harness recipe, and what YAML fields do I need?
evals.expected_output: Explains that CHAIN is opt-in and requires EVALUATE, that network must be testnet, that an ECDSA operator is supplied through environment variables, and that assertions must be flagged executableWithTestSigner to actually transact.
assertions: The output includes chainValidation: Names the chainValidation block
The output satisfies: States the network must be testnet
The output satisfies: Operator credentials come from environment variables
The output satisfies: Calls out that the operator must be ECDSA, not ED25519
The output includes executableWithTestSigner: Links chainValidation to executableWithTestSigner assertions
The output satisfies: States that CHAIN depends on EVALUATE

evals.prompt: My .harness/spec.yaml has an extend.baseline block, a contract: key, and no schemaVersion. I want to add a new page to the recipe — can you edit it for me?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a pre-v3 recipe, declines to treat it as loadable, explains that hedera-harness migrate is gone, and recommends rewriting to schemaVersion 3 (extend.baseline → baseline, contract: → eval:) or regenerating with init.
assertions: The output satisfies: Identifies the recipe as predating schema v3
The output satisfies: Does not recommend the removed migrate command as the path forward
The output satisfies: Explains extend.baseline → baseline and contract → eval

evals.prompt: I want the harness to build a whole HTS subscription feature: the token service layer, a management UI, and wallet-gated mint flows. Should that be one PRD or several?
evals.expected_output: Weighs a single PRD against ordered increments, recommends splitting only because this spans layers, explains that prd accepts a list delivered in order onto one branch, that each increment must leave the app green, and that eval: should be listed 1:1 with prd: so each slice is graded against its own checklist.
assertions: The output satisfies: Explains that prd can be an ordered list of increments
The output satisfies: Each increment must leave the app green on its own
The output satisfies: A failing increment stops the sequence
The output satisfies: Orders increments by dependency, not size
The output satisfies: Increments deliver onto a single branch
The output satisfies: Pairs eval: 1:1 with prd: for per-increment grading
